title: Draugr Village

# Draugr Village

Type: Point of interest | Internal ID: WoodVillage1 | Location: Meadows | Resources: Meadows chest, ,, Wild Beehive, ,, Finewood | Inhabitants: Draugr, ,, Draugr Elite

# Introduction

Draugr Villages are a Point of interest found in Meadows more than 2000m away from world center. It's a gathering of large wooded houses inhabited by Draugr and they always feature partial log wall perimeters.
Draugrs are generally locked inside houses and only emerge if the player opens the doors.
Furnitures inside house can be destroyed for Finewood.

## Great Hall

The great hall is the largest building in the village. Inside can be found up to 6 Chairs and a Raven throne, with a 50% chance each. At the center 6 stones mimic a Hearth. Up to 3 Meadows chests can be found under the wood floor beneath the body pile.
It is inhabited by a Body pile and one Draugr elite and up to 5 Draugrs with a 75% chance to spawn each.

## Great Hall Ruin

The great hall has a ruined version, with a missing roof. Inside can be found up to 3 Chairs, with a 50% chance each, and a Wild Beehive with a 33% chance.
It is inhabited by a Body pile and up to 3 Draugrs with a 75% chance each to spawn.

## House

The house is the most common structure. Inside, there is a 50% chance for a Meadows chest and a 20% chance for a Wild Beehive. Up to two unusable wood bed can also be found.
It is inhabited by 1 ranged Draugr and up to 2 melee Draugrs with a 75% chance each.

## Long House

The long house is a longer that regular house with a round roof. Inside, there are up to 3 Chairs and a Table with a 50% chance each. There is a 75% chance for a Meadows chest.
It is inhabited by a Body pile and up to 4 Draugrs and a Draugr elite with a 75% chance each.

### Long House Ruin

The ruined version of the long house also has up to 3 Chairs and a Table with a 50% chance each. No chest but a 33% chance for a Wild Beehive.
It is inhabited by a Body pile with a 50% chance and up to 2 Draugrs with a 75% chance each.

## Tower

The tower has a 33% chance for a wild beehive at the last floor.
The top is guarded by up to 2 ranged Draugrs with a 90% chance each. The first floor is guarded by up to 2 Draugrs with a 75% chance each.

### Tower Ruin

The ruined version of the tower is missing the upper half. It also has a 33% chance for a wild beehive and up to 2 Draugrs with a 50% chance each.

## Strategy

If the player can gain an elevated position over the houses -- either by building a small tower or getting on top of a roof -- they can often use a bow to shoot into the other buildings, providing them relative safety from the Draugr within. This is one of the safest ways to destroy the body piles found in some of the houses, in addition to being a somewhat safe method of dealing with any Draugr elite that spawn. Do note that all types of Draugr deal significant damage to wooden structures, and are able to tear buildings down beneath the player. Draugr Archers also represent a significant danger for players utilizing this strategy, especially those who are not equipped to deal with them.
Luring other hostile Creatures -- Boar, Greydwarfs, or even Trolls, for instance -- into the village is an effective, if short-lived, method of temporarily distracting the Draugr, as they will often disengage with the player to fight other creatures. This can buy the player some time to either escape or destroy the Body piles.
Since the indoor Draugr can not open doors, another strategy is to first kill the outdoor Draugr enemies and then use the AOE damage of the Stagbreaker to hit the body piles from outdoors. However, it is also possible to break the already weakened wooden walls and allow Draugr to come out.
